scope: Neutral, framework-agnostic 'how to fix' guidance keyed by control risk domain. Resolved for a failing control so an owner gets next steps, not just a finding. A per-control override may be added later; the default applies when a domain is not yet authored.

default.summary: Assign an owner, fix the underlying gap, and re-collect evidence so the control test passes on the next evaluation.
steps: Assign the failing control to an accountable owner with a due date.
Investigate the open finding(s) the control test reported and confirm the root cause.
Apply the fix at the source (configuration, policy, or process), not just the symptom.
Re-run the connector sync so fresh evidence is collected, then verify the control test returns to passing.

identity.summary: Tighten who can access what: enforce MFA, least privilege, key hygiene, and timely deprovisioning, then prove it with current identity evidence.
steps: Require MFA for every human (console) account; exempt only key-pair service identities and track them separately.
Remove standing privileged access in favor of least-privilege roles and just-in-time elevation.
Rotate or disable access keys older than the policy window and any that are unused.
Deprovision accounts for departed users and run a periodic access review to certify the rest.
references: CIS Controls v8 — 5 (Account Management), 6 (Access Control Management)

monitoring.summary: Make security-relevant activity observable: centralize logs, alert on the events that matter, and retain them long enough to investigate.
steps: Ship security and audit logs from every in-scope system to a central, access-controlled store.
Define alerts for the high-signal events (privileged use, auth failures, config changes) with an owner for triage.
Set a retention period that meets the applicable framework and your investigation needs.
Confirm collection is unbroken — a silent gap in monitoring is itself a finding.

data-protection.summary: Protect data by classification: encrypt it in transit and at rest, restrict access to it, and retain or dispose of it per policy.
steps: Classify the data store and confirm encryption in transit and at rest is enabled.
Scope access to the data to the minimum roles, and review that access periodically.
Apply the retention/disposal policy for the data's classification.
Re-collect the posture evidence for the affected store and verify the control test passes.

risk-management.summary: Run the risk loop: identify, assess, treat, and review risks on a defined cadence, with an accountable owner per risk.
steps: Record the risk in the register with severity, likelihood, and impact.
Choose a treatment (mitigate, transfer, accept) and assign an owner and due date.
For accepted risks, capture the rationale and an approver.
Re-assess on the defined cadence so the risk view stays current.

ai-governance.summary: Govern AI systems like any other asset: inventory them, map their context and dependencies, assign oversight, and document decisions.
steps: Add the AI system to an inventory with its purpose, owner, data sources, and dependencies.
Map its operating context and risks, and record the assessment.
Assign human oversight with the authority to pause or roll back the system.
Keep documentation current so the governance evidence reflects the deployed system.
references: NIST AI RMF — GOVERN & MAP functions
